### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`  _(via DashboardWidgetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via DashboardWidgetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via DashboardWidgetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39a912ea73ddff7fc85ebb3379a8ce74ff1343f5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cbad8adc60ff74b4c794971a08e21735217af3a3` — the merge of head `4435664b26cb01f1d1d4b6c9424dc6e799bbf2fa` into base `39a912ea73ddff7fc85ebb3379a8ce74ff1343f5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cbad8adc60ff74b4c794971a08e21735217af3a3 && git checkout cbad8adc60ff74b4c794971a08e21735217af3a3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 39a912ea73ddff7fc85ebb3379a8ce74ff1343f5 4435664b26cb01f1d1d4b6c9424dc6e799bbf2fa && git checkout -B drift-repro 39a912ea73ddff7fc85ebb3379a8ce74ff1343f5 && git merge --no-ff 4435664b26cb01f1d1d4b6c9424dc6e799bbf2fa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39a912ea73ddff7fc85ebb3379a8ce74ff1343f5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 39a912ea73ddff7fc85ebb3379a8ce74ff1343f5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b3b3c516f93786ae888815e6c2a8434abad3f3f1`
Local-runs: none

Isolated contract review of PR #21425 for card #21293, branch `claude/issue-21293-single-series-measure-arity`, net diff `origin/main...b3b3c516f9` (merge base `db3fee3dc9`): 10 files, +585/-86. Inputs: the card's body and its three comments (triage `5944795015`, the claim `5952561725`, the os-dev report `5954788000`); objectui#11417's ruling `5943580519`; the mother rule `11d28c17df` (PR #21053, #20958) as a git object; the PR body, its file list and the diff; the head's check-runs; and objectui read-only at the `.objectui-sha` pin `89cad75d5570` and at its `main` `e46ee770ba`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set at `DashboardWidgetSchema.values`, every door that parses the spec schema.** With `dimensions` declared and non-empty, two or more `values`, and `type` in `pie` / `donut` / `funnel` / `treemap` / `sankey`, the widget is refused: ONE `custom` issue at `values` naming the widget `id`, the count and the type (`dashboard.zod.ts`, the single-series arm inside `checkDashboardWidgetChartMeasureArity` at `:878`, chained once at `:1461`). **Right** — exactly the ruled narrowing, through #20958's check (same function, one more arm, same attachment point) with no second rule. The five live in the module-private `SINGLE_SERIES_CHART_TYPES` (`:784`, `as const satisfies readonly ChartType[]`), which the check, its message and the `values` doc string read.
2. **`scatter` and `radar` with a dimension and two or more measures still parse**: the single-series arm returns on any type outside the five before adding an issue. **Right** — outside the ruling, as the card and triage said. Named, not a defect of this PR: at the pin the renderer also binds `series[0]` on `scatter` (`AdvancedChartImpl.tsx:1338`, `:2464`) but says so on the chart, and `radar` maps every series (`:2418`). The ruling drew the line at the five; the diff keeps it there.
3. **#20958's dimensionless refusal is byte-identical.** The dimensionless `ctx.addIssue` block at the head equals the one on `origin/main` character for character (both extracted and compared). The arms are exclusive on `dimensions` — the single-series arm returns after its issue, and the dimensionless arm is reached only when `dimensions` is absent or `[]` — so a dimensionless widget of the five gets exactly one issue with the old text. The reordering of the early returns (metric family and `ChartTypeSchema` membership now precede the `dimensions` read) moves no dimensionless verdict, since every return is a pure predicate on the same inputs. **Right.**
4. **Unchanged answers, each read off the code**: one measure on every type (a `values` of one member, or none, returns first); every `DASHBOARD_WIDGET_MULTI_MEASURE_TYPES` member with or without a dimension (each arm returns on them); the metric family (returns before either arm, so the sibling check's one issue stands alone); a `type` outside `ChartTypeSchema` (returns); `values: []` (`.min(1)` untouched). **Right.**
5. **One input whose answer moves and that the ruling does not cover — direct calls only.** Called as a function with a non-array `dimensions` (a string, say) on one of the five with two measures, the old export returned silently ("anything but absent-or-empty returns"); the new one refuses, because the single-series arm treats anything but absent-or-empty as declared. Unreachable through the spec door (the field's own `invalid_type`) and through objectui's mirror, which re-types only `id` and `type` (`complex.zod.ts:1261`–`:1266` at the pin) and keeps the spec's `dimensions`. The direction matches the rule's own sentence ("one series whatever its `dimensions`"). Judged acceptable; named so it is not met later as an unannounced move.
6. **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec/ui`**: `checkDashboardWidgetDimensionlessMeasureArity` removed, `checkDashboardWidgetChartMeasureArity` added (`api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json`, one row out and one in each; the spec object's `.superRefine` count stays 3). A removed export is breaking on its own, and the changeset says so (②). **Necessary or a choice?** A choice — the ruling ordered the arm, not the name — but one inside the claim's envelope (`5952561725` listed the two listings "if an export moves" and conditioned `Clause-②` on an added row), and in the startup-stage shape: no alias, no re-export of the old name, no grace window, FROM → TO in the changeset. A name that says "dimensionless" on a check that now judges dimensioned widgets would misdirect the one consumer the export exists for, a mirror choosing what to chain. **Right.**
7. **Consumers of the old name, verified at the pin.** `git grep` over objectui at `89cad75d5570` for `DimensionlessMeasureArity` and `MULTI_MEASURE_TYPES`: 0 files. Control `checkDashboardWidgetMetricMeasureArity`: the import at `complex.zod.ts:23` and the chain at `:1304` (the two code hits the dev counted), plus tests, changesets and comments. The same readings hold on objectui `main` `e46ee770ba`. The mirror chains `checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder` and `checkDashboardWidgetMetricMeasureArity` only (`:1303`–`:1304`); its census (`spec-object-refinements-7715.test.ts:135`) reads the spec object's check count, unchanged at 3, and names neither chart-arity name. In this repository the old name survives only as history (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, the two entries' prose), the changeset's FROM → TO row, one code comment, and the test that pins its absence from the barrel. The `Console Pin Gate` was skipped on this head by its path filter (`packages/spec/src/**` is not in the `console` filter), so the pin's safety against the rename rests on this grep, reproduced here, not on a CI build of this PR; Post-Task Checklist #4's pre-merge check is met. **Right.**
8. **Renderer premise, verified at the pin.** `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`: the `pie` / `donut` arm opens at `:2087` and binds `series[0]?.dataKey` at `:2095`; `funnel` `:2160` / `:2161`; `treemap` `:2242` / `:2243`; `sankey` `:2277` / `:2278`–`:2279`. None reads another series. objectui's own `SINGLE_SERIES_CHART_FAMILIES` (`DatasetWidget.tsx:415`) names the same five. **Right.**
9. **Registry.** The new entry file `18.dashboard-widget-single-series-multi-measure-refused.ts` matches its generated region in `registry.ts` line for line; it sits in `step18` between `dashboard-widget-metric-family-...` and `dashboard-widget-stage-order-non-funnel-refused`, the id sort the builder derives ("Order is DERIVED, never declared"). PR #21399's `analytics-query-window-non-negative-integer` is present once at the head and once on `main`; all three siblings are present; the merge commit `b3b3c516f9` is the `os-regen-merge.sh` merge of `main` at `db3fee3dc9`. The amended #20958 text in the region equals its entry file's. Consistent by reading; `check:migration-registry` runs under `Lint & Repo Gates` on the head (state below). No stale projection exists: `spec-changes.json` and `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` are not in the tree on `main`, and the mother PR touched neither. **Right.**
10. **Tests and fixtures.** The `[#21293]` block pins the five refusals, the one-measure control, the two-dimension refusals, `scatter` / `radar` acceptance, the multi-measure controls, the taxonomy read off the door (refused at two measures with a dimension = metric family plus the five), the message, the dimensionless message word for word as one issue with the parse leg equal to the direct call, the metric family's own single issue, the direct-call legs, `DashboardSchema.widgets[]` travel, the doc string, and the old name's absence from the barrel with the new export as the lit control. The `[#17779]` parse leg now runs on the ten types no check refuses, and its claim ("the metric check leaves non-metric types alone") is read off the metric export directly for all fifteen, so no claim was dropped. The catalogue row "two measures on a `pie` WITH a dimension — out of this rule" became five refusing rows plus accepting rows for `scatter`, `radar` and a one-measure `pie`. Every pin whose premise the ruling falsified moved to the refusal; none was deleted. **Right.**
11. **Doc string and the generated reference** (`dashboard.mdx`, the `values` row in both tables): state the single-series rule and read the private constant. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right.** `(narrowing)`: the accept set at `values` shrinks — that is the change, and it is BREAKING, so the banner is owed. `yes`: the claim's own criterion was "yes if the diff adds any export-listing row", and the listing gains `checkDashboardWidgetChartMeasureArity (function)` while losing the old row (which is why T3 stays silent). The five T2 tells the dev reports on `SINGLE_SERIES_CHART_TYPES` are members of a module-private narrowing set: false as widenings, and the arm does not rest on them. The gate itself was not re-run here; the dev's reading is consistent with the diff.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/21293-single-series-multi-measure-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, a **BREAKING** banner, and exactly one marker, `adr-0087: registered dashboard-widget-single-series-multi-measure-refused`. Same shape as the mother rule's changeset (`minor` plus banner plus `registered`, under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major` enforces). `Check Changeset` is green on the head. **Right.**
- **Every sentence checked against the diff and the pin.** The export swap (one row out, one in, both listings) holds. The renderer binding on the four arms holds at the pin lines above. "Parsed before the change on all five, and on `scatter` / `radar` / `bar` / `table`" holds by the old code's early return on any non-empty `dimensions`. "Refused after at `widgets[N].values`; `scatter` and `radar` parse as before" holds. The FROM → TO table's four rows hold: the import row names the right subpath (`@objectstack/spec/ui`, per `export-origins/ui.json`) and the same `(widget, ctx)` signature. "ONE `custom` issue ... draws one series whatever its `dimensions`" matches the message text. "No first-party consumer chained the old name; the mirror chains `checkDashboardWidgetStageOrder` and `checkDashboardWidgetMetricMeasureArity` only, at the pin and on main" holds. The "Nothing else moves" list holds item by item (one measure; `scatter` / `radar`; the multi-measure set with or without a dimension; the dimensionless five word for word and one issue; the metric family; `too_small`; a type outside `ChartTypeSchema`). The census figures (496 / 33 / 1 here; 480 / 13 / 1 in objectui) are the dev's measurement and were not re-run; the one spec fixture they name is visible in the diff, and the objectui hit they name is prose in `.changeset/11417-dashboard-single-series-dropped-measure.md` at the pin.
- **Does the ADR-0087 disposition cover the removed name?** Yes. The entry's `surface` names the export and its rename, and its `replacement` tells a mirror that chained the old name to import the new one. An export rename is a TypeScript-surface change whose channel is the consumer's compiler (ADR-0087 D8), so the changeset's FROM → TO row is the load-bearing prescription for it; the entry carries it as a rider on the metadata narrowing it registers. One marker is the gate's rule; one entry covering both facets is **right**.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The amended #20958 entry, outside the claim's listed surface.** Two sentences in `18.dashboard-widget-dimensionless-multi-measure-refused.ts` that this diff made false — the export's name, and "the same seven types WITH a dimension keep accepting several measures exactly as before" — now name the new export (recording the old one) and point the five at the new entry; the registry region was regenerated, not hand-edited. **Judged right.** The repo's rules for registered entries: the entries README forbids hand edits inside the registry markers (respected) and derives the filename from the id so that two cards editing one entry collide in git (respected — `main` was merged through `os-regen-merge.sh`); it does not freeze an entry's prose. ADR-0087's "appended to, never rewritten" is `sys_metadata_history`, not entry text. Leaving the sentence would have `os migrate meta` print, in the same protocol-18 hop, that dimensioned pies "keep accepting" beside the entry that refuses them — a declared-but-not-delivered statement Prime Directive #10 forbids. The standing clause the dev followed exists: `.claude/agents/os-dev.md:67` (a published defect this round's change makes false must be fixed) and `:184`–`:185` (when the dispatch wording conflicts with that file, the file wins and the conflict is named in the report, never chosen silently). The claim's "stop on breach" was answered by naming the conflict in the report. Two sentences, one hop, no new rule: no scope expansion. **Answered.**
2. **Commit trailer.** The two pushed non-merge commits (`c1d4f3dd`, `221df98d`) end with the model-free trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes (the session-URL line and the generic co-author line, neither naming a model); the merge commit `b3b3c516f9` is `os-regen-merge.sh`'s `git merge --no-edit` product and carries no trailer; no model identifier appears in the pushed history, the PR title or body, the changeset, the entries or the code. **Answered; no deviation stands.**
3. **T2 tells on a module-private `as const` array.** **Answered**: they are not widenings, and the declaration does not rest on them. Escalated as a note for the adopting seat, not filed (this review files nothing): `check-widening-tells` reads every new bare member of an `as const` array on `packages/spec/src/**` as "the accept set gains a value", with a licence only for ledger-table rows; a future PR that adds a module-private NARROWING set with no export change would meet exit 4 under a truthful `no (narrowing)`. That is a gate-imprecision question, not a defect in this diff.
4. **The module-private set beside objectui's `SINGLE_SERIES_CHART_FAMILIES`.** **Answered: acceptable.** The ruling's "follows it by reference" is the check export (what the mirror chains), and the refusal prints the five, so the mirror never restates them to refuse correctly; objectui's set is renderer-derived and tied to the renderer by its own test (`DatasetWidget.singleSeriesMeasures-11417.test.tsx`). Two lists exist, in two repositories, kept honest from different ends. Noted for the seat: the mother rule exported its set so the mirror could import rather than restate it, whereas this PR followed the metric family's private precedent (`SINGLE_MEASURE_WIDGET_TYPES`); exporting later is a free widening (a T3 row, `yes (widening)`), so nothing is foreclosed.
5. `open_questions` is empty; the two `out_of_scope_findings` are items 3 and 4 above. Of the dispatch's hypotheses, H3 "partly falsified" (no declared order; the builder sorts by id) is correct and changes nothing in the landing.

**Check-runs on the head**, read over REST at 2026-10-02T14:56Z after the last shard concluded: 35 check-runs, 33 `success`, 2 `skipped`, none failed, none still running. The skips are `Console Pin Gate` (its `console` path filter does not include `packages/spec/src/**`; see ①.7 for the pin reading that stands in for it) and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`. Green on this head: `Lint & Repo Gates` (carrying `check:migration-registry`, `check:api-surface`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and the widening-tells gate), `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, all six `Test Core` shards, every `Type Check` leg, the three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI` and `Temporal Conformance`. These conclusions are the gate verdicts this record relies on; nothing was re-run locally. The PR touches no governed surface, so this record is the Clause-② contract review the claim called for, not a Tier S landing record.
